givtcp_entities_missing.title: GivTCP entities not found
givtcp_entities_missing.description:
These GivTCP entities, configured during setup, are no longer in Home Assistant: {entities}. This usually means GivTCP was reinstalled with a different inverter serial, was upgraded and renamed or removed entities, or its entity ids changed. The integration looks each one up again by its registry id, and these could not be found.

To fix: go to **Settings → Devices & Services → GivEnergy Inverter Manager**, open the menu and select **Reconfigure**, then use the entities it finds or choose them by hand.

min_soc_too_high.title: Battery minimum SoC is set too high
min_soc_too_high.description:
**Battery minimum SoC** is currently {min_soc}%. On nights when charging is skipped, the integration writes this value as the inverter's charge target. A value this high causes the inverter to hold the battery at {min_soc}% all night, importing from the grid instead of discharging.

Recommended value: 10–20%. Go to **Settings → Devices & Services → GivEnergy Inverter Manager → Configure**, tick **Battery and charging** and lower the battery minimum charge.

confirm.title: Clear the other charge slots
confirm.description:
The integration manages charge slot 1 only. These other slots also have a charge window: {slots}.

The inverter charges in every active slot, so a leftover slot can charge the battery at a dearer rate than the cheapest period.

Selecting **Submit** sets the start and end time of each of them to 00:00. Slot 1 is not changed. You can also clear them yourself in GivTCP.

abort.dry_run: Dry run is on, so nothing was changed. Turn off the Dry run switch (on the device page or the dashboard's Settings) to clear the slots.
abort.write_failed: GivTCP did not accept every write. The slots that are still active stay listed. Check that GivTCP is running, then try again.
abort.not_loaded: GivEnergy Inverter Manager is not loaded. Reload it, then try again.

confirm.title: Set the battery cost
confirm.description:
**Battery cost** is 0, so battery wear is not counted and Net Saving Today equals Saving vs Grid Today. Enter what the battery cost to put a wear cost on each kWh cycled.

The value is saved to the integration options, and the integration reloads. Every other saved option stays as it is. Dismiss this repair if you do not want wear counted.

data_description.battery_cost_eur: What the battery cost, including installation. Must be above 0.

error.cost_required: Enter a cost above 0, or dismiss this repair.

abort.not_loaded: GivEnergy Inverter Manager is not loaded. Reload it, then try again.

ev_charging_at_base_rate.title: EV is charging at the base rate
ev_charging_at_base_rate.description:
The car is drawing about {power_kw} kW from the grid at the {rate_name} rate. A cheaper band starts at {next_cheap_start}.

Moving the session into the cheaper band lowers its cost. Pause the charge now and resume it when the cheaper band starts, or set the charger's own schedule. This integration does not stop or pause the charger.

The repair clears when the session ends or the rate drops. Ignore it to hide it for the rest of the session.

write_not_confirmed.title: The inverter did not take a charge setting
write_not_confirmed.description:
The integration wrote a charge setting to GivTCP and read it back after every attempt, and the inverter still showed the old value. Not taken: {settings}.

The inverter keeps its old charge window or target until this is fixed, so tonight's charge may not follow the plan.

The usual causes are that GivTCP's **Real Time Control** setting is off (an upgrade of GivTCP can reset it), or that GivTCP is not running or not publishing. Also check that GivTCP's day rate, night rate and tariff type are filled in. The learn more link has the steps.

The repair clears when a later write, or a later look, finds each setting at its value. Ignore it to hide it until then.

givtcp_feed_frozen.title: GivTCP has stopped updating
givtcp_feed_frozen.description:
GivTCP's solar, battery and load entities in Home Assistant still show their last values, but none has been reported since {last_reported}. They are not unavailable, so nothing else shows a fault.

The integration has stopped planning, stopped writing to the inverter and made its own entities unavailable, because it would act on readings that no longer move. It resumes by itself when GivTCP reports again.

Check that GivTCP is running and has not crashed (an upgrade can leave it stopped), that MQTT is connected, and that GivTCP's day rate, night rate and tariff type are filled in. Also check that **Real Time Control** is on, because an upgrade of GivTCP can reset it. The learn more link has the steps.

givtcp_not_answering.title: GivTCP is not getting data from the inverter

tariff_review_due.title: Tariff rates have not been reviewed

confirm.title: Confirm the tariff rates
confirm.description:
The tariff rates were last saved or confirmed on {last_reviewed}, {days} days ago. A supplier price change leaves every cost figure wrong until the rates here are updated.

Check the rates against your latest bill. If a rate changed, go to **Settings → Devices & Services → GivEnergy Inverter Manager → Configure**, tick **Tariff** and save the new rates, or tick **Schedule a rate change** to give them a start date. If the rates are correct, select **Submit** to confirm them.

abort.not_loaded: GivEnergy Inverter Manager is not loaded. Reload it, then try again.

confirm.title: Confirm the system
confirm.description:
Since the integration last looked, this changed: {changes}.

This happens after GivTCP is upgraded, an inverter is added or replaced, or a battery module is added or removed. The integration keeps managing the inverter it was set up with and has not changed anything.

If the entities it uses have been renamed or have gone, open **Reconfigure** from the integration's menu first and use the entities it finds. Then select **Submit** to say this is the system to manage. Dismiss this repair to be asked again after the next change.

abort.not_loaded: GivEnergy Inverter Manager is not loaded. Reload it, then try again.

givtcp_real_time_control_off.title: GivTCP's Real Time Control is off
givtcp_real_time_control_off.description:
GivTCP's **Real Time Control** switch has read off for several minutes. While it is off, GivTCP accepts a change from Home Assistant and does not send it to the inverter, so the charge window and target the integration writes never reach it. The inverter keeps its old settings and tonight's charge may not follow the plan.

An upgrade of GivTCP can reset this setting.

To fix: open GivTCP's settings (for the add-on, **Settings → Add-ons → GivTCP → Configuration**), turn **Real Time Control** on, save and restart GivTCP. This repair clears by itself when the switch reads on.

givtcp_resets_entity_ids.title: This GivTCP release resets entity ids
givtcp_resets_entity_ids.description:
GivTCP reports version {version}. GivTCP 3.6 and 3.6.1 delete and recreate an entity when its discovery settings change, so Home Assistant gives it the default entity id again and it loses its name and area. {fixed_in} fixed this, and releases before 3.6 do not do it.

The integration finds an entity again under its new id by itself, so it keeps working, but your own dashboards and automations that use a renamed entity can break.

To fix: update the GivTCP add-on to {fixed_in} or later, then restart it. This repair clears by itself once GivTCP reports a newer version. The integration has not changed anything.

charge_blocked_by_pause.title: The battery pause stops tonight's charge
charge_blocked_by_pause.description:
GivTCP's battery pause stops the battery charging from {pause}, and tonight's charge window ({window}) falls inside it. The integration writes the window and the target, and the inverter reports them as set, but it does not charge while the pause is on, so the battery will not reach the target.

To fix: in GivTCP, set the **Battery pause mode** to `Disabled` or `PauseDischarge`, or move the pause so it does not cover the charge window. The integration never changes the pause. This repair clears by itself when the pause no longer covers the window.

dashboard_out_of_date.title: The GivEnergy dashboard is out of date

confirm.title: Update the GivEnergy dashboard
confirm.description:
The dashboard at /{url_path} no longer matches the dashboard the integration builds now. This happens after an upgrade, after a device is added or removed, or after the dashboard was edited.

Select **Submit** to replace the stored layout of /{url_path} with the current one. Your own edits to that dashboard are replaced too. Its current configuration is saved first to `{backup_file}` in the configuration folder.

Ignore this repair to keep the dashboard as it is.

abort.not_loaded: GivEnergy Inverter Manager is not loaded. Reload it, then try again.
abort.dashboard_url_path_missing: No dashboard is kept up to date any more. Run the update_dashboard action with the dashboard's URL path.
abort.dashboard_not_found: The dashboard no longer exists. Run the update_dashboard action with the URL path of another dashboard.
abort.dashboard_not_storage: The dashboard is now a YAML dashboard, so the integration does not change it.
abort.dashboard_recovery_mode: Home Assistant is in recovery mode, so dashboards cannot be saved. Restart normally and try again.
abort.config_file_write_failed: The old configuration could not be saved to the backup file, so the dashboard was not changed. Check that Home Assistant can write to the configuration folder.

config_entry_not_ready.message: First data fetch failed. Check that GivTCP is running and MQTT is connected. ({error})

givtcp_unavailable.message: GivTCP is not publishing data — solar and battery sensors are unavailable. Check that GivTCP is running and MQTT is connected.

givtcp_frozen.message: GivTCP is not updating. Its entities still hold their last values, but none has been reported recently. Check that GivTCP is running and MQTT is connected.

givtcp_not_answering.message: GivTCP is not getting data from the inverter, so its values are old. Check that the inverter is on and reachable, and that GivTCP is not paused.

no_config_entry.message: GivEnergy Inverter Manager is not configured. Add the integration in Settings → Integrations before calling this service.

config_file_write_failed.message: Failed to write the file to the Home Assistant config directory. Check that HA has write access to the config folder.

test_instance_dry_run_locked.message: Dry run cannot be turned off on a test instance. Delete the .givenergy_test_instance file from the Home Assistant configuration folder and restart Home Assistant to go live.

dashboard_update_needs_admin.message: Only a Home Assistant administrator can update the dashboard.

dashboard_url_path_missing.message: Give the URL path of the dashboard to update, such as dashboard-energy. No dashboard has been updated before, so there is none to reuse.

dashboard_not_found.message: There is no dashboard at /{url_path}. Create one with Settings → Dashboards → Add dashboard → New dashboard from scratch, then give the part of its address after the first slash.

dashboard_not_storage.message: The dashboard at /{url_path} is a YAML dashboard, so its configuration is a file the integration does not change. Pick a dashboard made in Settings → Dashboards, or use get_dashboard_yaml with Write file instead.

dashboard_recovery_mode.message: Home Assistant is in recovery mode, so dashboards cannot be saved. Restart normally and try again.

suggest_appliance_run.name: Suggest appliance run time
suggest_appliance_run.description: Checks whether now is a good time to run a high-load appliance (washing machine, dishwasher, etc.) based on current solar surplus, battery state, and the active tariff rate. Creates a persistent notification with the verdict and the reason. The action does not return a response.

appliance_name.name: Appliance name
appliance_name.description: Name of the appliance (used in the notification)

appliance_power_w.name: Appliance power (W)
appliance_power_w.description: Rated power consumption of the appliance in watts

get_roi_summary.name: Get ROI summary
get_roi_summary.description: Returns return-on-investment figures for today, this week, this month and this year, plus battery cycles and remaining life. Use response_variable to read the result in a script or automation. Returns an empty response until the first update has completed.

compare_tariff.name: Compare tariff
compare_tariff.description: Compares this bill period against a flat-rate alternative tariff, using the kWh imported and exported so far this period. Both tariffs are billed the same way: energy, supplier saving, standing charge, PSO levy, VAT, then the export credit. The alternative uses your tariff's supplier discount, VAT and PSO levy unless you enter your own. With more than one entry set up, the response lists every entry. Use response_variable to read the result.

rate.name: Import rate
rate.description: Flat import rate of the alternative tariff, per kWh

standing_charge.name: Standing charge per day
standing_charge.description: Daily standing charge of the alternative tariff

export_rate.name: Export rate
export_rate.description: Export rate of the alternative tariff, per kWh

discount_rate.name: Supplier discount
discount_rate.description: Supplier discount of the alternative tariff in percent. Leave empty to use your tariff's discount

vat_rate.name: VAT rate
vat_rate.description: VAT of the alternative tariff in percent. Leave empty to use your tariff's VAT rate

pso_levy.name: PSO levy
pso_levy.description: PSO levy of the alternative tariff for a whole bill period. Leave empty to use your tariff's PSO levy

year_on_year_summary.name: Year-on-year summary
year_on_year_summary.description: Compares this bill period with the same period one year ago. The comparison needs 12 completed bill periods. Until then the response has no_data set to true and shows how many periods are stored. Use response_variable to read the result.

export_energy_data.name: Export energy data
export_energy_data.description: Writes today, yesterday, this week, this month, this year and each stored completed bill period to givenergy_energy_export.csv in the Home Assistant config directory, then shows a persistent notification. The action does not return a response.

get_dashboard_yaml.name: Get dashboard YAML
get_dashboard_yaml.description: Returns the GivEnergy dashboard as YAML text, the same dashboard the strategy builds. Use it as a fallback when the GivEnergy dashboard shows "Timeout waiting for strategy element". Copy the `yaml` value into a new dashboard's raw configuration editor, or turn on Write file and point a YAML dashboard at `givenergy_dashboard.yaml` in the configuration folder. Run it again after you add or remove a device, because a copy does not update itself. The tariff and bill tables follow your tariff and your bill. The Settings view is included only when an administrator runs the action.

write_file.name: Write file
write_file.description: Also write the YAML to `givenergy_dashboard.yaml` in the configuration folder, replacing it. The response then holds the path in `file`.

update_dashboard.name: Update dashboard
update_dashboard.description: Writes the GivEnergy dashboard into a dashboard you made with Settings → Dashboards → Add dashboard → New dashboard from scratch. It replaces that dashboard's whole configuration, your own edits included, after saving the old configuration to `givenergy_dashboard_backup.yaml` in the configuration folder. The integration remembers the dashboard, and a repair offers the same update when the dashboard is out of date. Only an administrator can run it.

url_path.name: Dashboard URL path
url_path.description: The part of the dashboard's address after the first slash, such as `dashboard-energy` for `/dashboard-energy`. Leave it empty to update the dashboard written last time.
